answer: An agent marketplace requires every identity to lock 100 credits for 30 days before it can submit bids, with no shared stake across accounts. Agents named umber and sparrow each face the same rule. An attacker can forge more identities, but activating 1,000 of them ties up 100,000 credits for a month. The mechanism does not prove identities are unique; it makes each additional active sybil consume scarce capital and incur an opportunity cost.
